_purpose: Phase 5E. Frozen protocol for the generalisation test on a two-asset weighted basket Asian digital under correlated GBM. Fixed-N, reference-free (all estimators unbiased, so MSE = variance over independent Owen scramblings). Committed before the study is run.
payoff: 1{w1 mean_i S1_{t_i} + w2 mean_i S2_{t_i} >= K}, smoothed by integrating out the common first-step direction Z0 = (Z1 + Z2)/sqrt(2(1+rho)); z* by Newton
gradients: central finite differences of the smooth per-path integrands, h = 1e-4 (basket.fd_gradients); training and evaluation use independent random streams

rotations.pca: eigenvectors of the residual path covariance (baseline, no training)
rotations.joint6: trace-normalised sum over all six Greeks

scales: per-path plain-MC standard deviation of each smoothed Greek, from 2^19 independent paths

hypotheses.E1: The gradient covariance of every Greek stays close to rank one (top-eigenvalue share >= 0.90), as in the one-asset contract. Expected to weaken, because the smoothed integrand now depends on two path averages.
hypotheses.E2: The top gradient directions of Greeks of the same asset are aligned (|cos| >= 0.90); those of different assets (delta1 vs delta2 etc.) need not be.
hypotheses.E3: One joint rotation over all six Greeks costs at most a factor 1.25 in variance for any single Greek relative to that Greek's own rotation (geometric mean over scenarios).
hypotheses.E4: Greek-aware rotations still reduce variance relative to path PCA (ratio < 1). Whether the gain is smaller than for the one-asset contract (Phase 4: 3-20x) is reported.
hypotheses.E5: Model-based break-even number of valuations is reported from the measured training cost, the measured cost per point and the fixed-N loss ratio (variance ~ N^-alpha). It is a model estimate, not a timed experiment.
